claim: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm).

claim: The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris, France.
notes: Established geographical landmark.

notes: Official Brexit completion date.

claim: Penicillin was discovered by Scottish physician Alexander Fleming in 1928.
notes: Historic medical discovery.

claim: The Great Barrier Reef is situated off the north-east coast of Australia.
notes: Geographic location of the world's largest coral reef.

claim: Albert Einstein won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.
notes: Nobel committee citation for Einstein.

claim: NASA's Perseverance rover successfully landed on Mars in Jezero Crater in February 2021.
notes: Perseverance landed February 18, 2021.

claim: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean basin on Earth.
notes: Well-established physical geographic fact.

claim: Drinking silver nitrate or bleach cures diabetes and eliminates high blood sugar permanently.
notes: Dangerous medical hoax debunked by FDA and medical consensus.

claim: The Moon landing in 1969 was completely staged by NASA in a Nevada film studio directed by Stanley Kubrick.
notes: Debunked Apollo 11 conspiracy theory.

claim: 5G mobile network towers directly emit biological COVID-19 viruses into the atmosphere.
notes: Debunked conspiracy theory connecting telecommunications with viral pathogens.

claim: Eating bananas with milk creates a toxic poison that causes sudden cardiac arrest.
notes: Unfounded viral dietary hoax.

claim: Scientists confirmed that the Earth is hollow and inhabited by an advanced civilization at the core.
notes: Disproven hollow earth pseudoscience myth.

claim: Microwaving an iPhone for 30 seconds activates a hidden feature that fully recharges its battery.
notes: Known 'Apple Wave' hoax that destroys smartphones.

claim: The Great Wall of China is the only human-made structure visible from Mars with the naked eye.
notes: Common misconception debunked by NASA; not visible even from low Earth orbit without magnification.

claim: Vaccines contain microscopic RFID tracking microchips manufactured by Bill Gates to control human minds.
notes: Widely debunked conspiracy theory with no factual basis.

claim: Barack Obama was born in Kenya and forged his birth certificate to become US President.
notes: Debunked 'birther' claim; official certified birth certificate confirms Honolulu, Hawaii.

claim: Antarctica has secret tropical rainforests where live dinosaurs are currently being guarded by the United Nations.
notes: Fabricated conspiracy myth.

claim: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) will definitely achieve human-level consciousness and replace 100% of human jobs by 2030.
notes: Unverifiable future prediction and speculative claim.

claim: Drinking coffee daily reduces the overall risk of mortality in all humans.
notes: Observational studies show associations with longevity, but not universal or causal across all populations.

claim: A single glass of red wine every evening is universally beneficial for heart health.
notes: Conflicting scientific evidence; recent WHO and cardiology guidelines show risks of alcohol may outweigh benefits.

claim: Extraterrestrial intelligent beings have visited Earth and are currently in secret contact with world governments.
notes: Unproven and unverified; no verified public empirical evidence exists.

claim: Organic food is definitively more nutritious and contains significantly higher vitamin levels than conventional food.
notes: Mixed scientific evidence; systematic reviews find minor differences in certain antioxidants but no conclusive overall nutritional superiority.
